items.name: waterfall training / 滝行 / 修行
items.description:
The English description is translated below the Japanese one at DeepL.

滝の下で冷たい水を浴びることによる精神的な修行を行うLoRAです。

トリガーワードは　waterfall training　です。

重みは0.8前後推奨。

トリガーだけでも滝付近に出現はしますが waterfall, water, own hands together, wet, wading, wet clothes, partially submerged, see-through, wet hair, showering, splashing, closed eyes, palms together 辺りからお好みのものを入れていただき後は立たせたりあぐらをかかせればそれっぽいです。

Illustrious-XL 0.1をベースとして学習していますので他のIllustriousマージモデルやNoobマージモデルでも使用できる可能性はありますが検証は行っておりません。

以下翻訳

LoRA is a spiritual practice that involves bathing in cold water under a waterfall.

The trigger word is “waterfall training.”

Weight is recommended to be around 0.8.

Even with just the trigger, it will appear near the waterfall, but you can add your preferred keywords from the following list: waterfall, water, hands together, wet, wading, wet clothes, partially submerged, see-through, wet hair, showering, splashing, closed eyes, palms together, etc. Then, you can make it stand or sit in a cross-legged position to achieve the desired effect.

This model is trained using Illustrious-XL 0.1 as a base, so it may be compatible with other Illustrious merge models or Noob merge models, but we have not verified this.

items.name: SDXL-Waterfalls
items.description:
Lora focused on waterfalls. Trained on a set of 104 images from around the globe of different styles of waterfalls.

This early version isn't super great, as most SDXL checkpoints are focused on people rather than landscapes, but it is a decent starting point.

Recommend a moderate CFG (I've been using 13) and 40-60 steps. I've had good luck with several checkpoints including: base SDXL, cinemaxAlphaSDXL, MiaModel, TalmendoxSDXL.

~ Vixon's recipe for Focaccia Bread ~

Ingredients

4 cups all-purpose flour

2 teaspoons kosher salt

2 teaspoons instant yeast

2 cups lukewarm water

butter for greasing

4 tablespoons olive oil, divided

flaky sea salt

1 to 2 teaspoons whole rosemary leaves, optional

Instructions

In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and instant yeast. Add the water. Using a rubber spatula, mix until the liquid is absorbed and the ingredients form a sticky dough ball. Rub the surface of the dough lightly with olive oil. Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel, cloth bowl cover, or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator immediately for at least 12 hours or for as long as three days.

NOTE: It is important the dough really be slicked with olive oil especially if you are using a cloth bowl cover or tea towel as opposed to plastic wrap or a hard lid. If you are using a tea towel, consider securing it with a rubber band to make a more airtight cover. If you do not slick the dough with enough oil, you risk the dough drying out and forming a crust over the top layer.

Line two 8- or 9-inch pie plates or a 9×13-inch pan with parchment paper or grease with butter or coat with nonstick cooking spray.

Pour a tablespoon of oil into the center of each pan or 2 tablespoons of oil if using the 9×13-inch pan. Using two forks, deflate the dough by releasing it from the sides of the bowl and pulling it toward the center. Rotate the bowl in quarter turns as you deflate, turning the mass into a rough ball. Use the forks to split the dough into two equal pieces (or do not split if using the 9×13-inch pan). Place one piece into one of the prepared pans. Roll the dough ball in the oil to coat it all over, forming a rough ball. Repeat with the remaining piece. Let the dough balls rest for 3 to 4 hours depending on the temperature of your kitchen.

Set a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat it to 425°F. If using the rosemary, sprinkle it over the dough. Pour a tablespoon of oil over each round of dough (or two tablespoons if using a 9×13-inch pan). Rub your hands lightly in the oil to coat, then, using all of your fingers, press straight down to create deep dimples. If necessary, gently stretch the dough as you dimple to allow the dough to fill the pan. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt all over.

Transfer the pans or pan to the oven and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp. Remove the pans or pan from the oven and transfer the focaccia to a cooling rack. Let it cool for 10 minutes before cutting and serving; let it cool completely if you are halving it with the intention of making a sandwich.

items.name: Narrow waterfall
items.description:
A 'narrow waterfall' is a type of waterfall that has a relatively small width or breadth compared to other waterfalls. Waterfalls come in various shapes and sizes and can vary significantly in width. A narrow waterfall typically signifies water flowing down a relatively confined channel or rock formation.

When standing at the base of a waterfall and immersing yourself in the water cascading from above, exercise caution regarding floating debris. In particular, wood, which has a lower density than water, can float, and the potential energy generated by the difference in height can pose a risk of injury.

~ Vixon's recipe for Chocolate Pudding ~

Ingredients

1 ⅓ cup granulated sugar

⅔ cup unsweetened cocoa powder

⅓ cup cornstarch

pinch salt

4 ½ cups milk

3 tablespoons unsalted butter

1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Instructions

In a saucepan, combine sugar, cocoa powder, salt, and cornstarch. Mix well. Add in cold milk, whisk until combined.

Increase heat to medium, stirring constantly until mixture reaches a boil. Remove the pudding from the heat as soon as it begins to boil and thicken. If left to continue boiling the starch will start to break down and it will not properly thicken, resulting in watery pudding.

As soon as the pudding has thickened, remove from the heat and stir in butter and vanilla.

Allow mixture to cool completely, stirring occasionally to avoid a skin forming on the pudding.

Serve chilled or warm.

notes

Place a plastic wrap directly on the surface of the pudding while it cools to avoid a skin from forming.

items.description: I've transformed the scene of my favorite person being swept away by a waterfall into a Lora. This includes two angles: one where they're on the brink of falling from the top of the waterfall, and another where they're being gently swept by a milder waterfall. I initially wanted to create a wide shot of them falling from a distance, but the water didn't seem to flow naturally from top to bottom, so I abandoned that idea. Now, the Lora focuses more on close-up images of the person falling.

🔷 ZenRush: Mystical Anime Adventure – Version Introduction

🌀 Version 1.0 – "Path of the Seeker"
The first release of ZenRush focuses on high-energy anime adventure, blending fast movement, cinematic action, and ancient temple exploration. This version is optimized for dynamic poses, running, biking, parkour, and mystical environments like hidden monasteries, misty waterfalls, and sacred ruins.

🔹 Key Features:
✅ Dynamic Action – Running, biking, jumping, escaping, and fast-paced adventure scenes.
✅ Mystical Settings – Buddhist temples, glowing lanterns, ancient stone carvings, and hidden pathways.
✅ Cinematic Anime Aesthetic – Motion blur, deep lighting effects, fog, and environmental storytelling.
✅ Balanced Character Diversity – Unique face structures, hairstyles, and varied outfits to avoid repetition.

🔹 Trained On:

  • Anime-style action poses for natural movement.

  • Diverse lighting conditions (moonlight, sunset, stormy weather, temple glow).

  • Fantasy adventure themes inspired by classic anime exploration stories.

🔹 Best Used With:

  • Base Model: Anything V5 / AbyssOrangeMix3 / Counterfeit V3

  • Resolution: 512x512 or higher for best detail.

  • Trigger Words: dynamic action pose, hidden monastery entrance, misty waterfall passag
